title: Interface to the proved strict tensor and Hom representative calculations
statement: For the strict tensor and product-Hom models of [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models, def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation], use the actual sheafification-unit pure tensors and the canonical isomorphism Tot(single_0(T) tensor B) = T tensor B termwise. This isomorphism sends each tensorGenerator to its ordinary pure tensor. Maps from this tensor complex into a product Hom component agree if every pure-tensor evaluation agrees. Postcomposition of a Hom section evaluates as postcomposition of its value. The sheaf tensor is preadditive. The fixed resolution augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and its target is K-injective [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; resolved Hom preserves quasi-isomorphisms. In an abelian monoidal preadditive category, tensor by a finite product of units preserves finite limits, including rank zero. When tensor commutes with a specified exact colimit, tensor by that colimit preserves finite limits if tensor by every diagram object does. These are named interfaces to existing proved calculations, with no changed representatives.

source.place: Tags 0A8X, 0A95 and 06YN; the already proved strict representative calculations of DerivedInternalHomFilteredColimitData, InternalHomFiniteFreeStage and InternalHomFilteredContinuity, exposed as a named interface.

proof.text: Use the sheafification-unit pure tensor and the canonical total-tensor/single-complex isomorphism. The existing pure-tensor calculation proves its generator formula. Pure tensors generate the sheaf tensor product; the product Hom projections and evaluation on slices detect all target sections. Apply the existing tensorGenerator_hom_ext calculation. Naturality of each Hom-product projection gives postcomposition evaluation.

Reuse the proved monoidal preadditivity and functorial K-injective resolution properties in the strict-model data module. Resolved Hom takes quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, by that module's existing homFixedQuasiIso theorem. These interface theorems change no constructions.

Expose the existing general exactness calculations: tensor by a finite product of units preserves finite limits, including rank zero; tensor by a colimit of such exact tensor functors preserves finite limits when tensor commutes with the colimit and that colimit is exact. Apply the proved private calculations in the finite-free and filtered-continuity modules.

theorem tensorGenerator_hom_ext (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v r})
    (T : Modules.{u, v, r} J R)
    (B P Q : CochainComplex (Modules.{u, v, r} J R) ℤ) (n m : ℤ)
    (a b : ((tensor.{u, v, r} J R).obj (T, B)).X n ⟶
      (homComplex (R := R) P Q).X m)
    (h : ∀ (p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + m = q) (U : Cᵒᵖ)
      (t : T.val.obj U) (z : (B.X n).val.obj U) (x : (P.X p).val.obj U),
      homValue.{u, v, r} J R P Q m p q hpq U
          (a.val.app U (tensorGenerator.{u, v, r} J R T B n U t z)) x =
        homValue.{u, v, r} J R P Q m p q hpq U
          (b.val.app U (tensorGenerator.{u, v, r} J R T B n U t z)) x) : a = b
